text:
Hello kennel team,
Thanks for a balanced handover; the relief planner mentioned a point about quiet corners

I am looping this through from the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways so the next shift stays steady and the animal side stays calm. Please keep the handling pace unhurried, use soft voices, and keep carriers settled where the noise stays low. If a traveler arrives with a nervous pet, bring the welfare coordinator in early and keep the notes tight but complete. The goal is simple: reduce stress, avoid mixed signals, and keep the desk moving without making the animal work harder than it needs to.

For the cat files, <<FACT F055>> Please keep the wording plain when you brief the traveler, and do not add extra commentary that could confuse the handoff. For the bird cases, <<FACT F065>> and <<FACT F077>> so the desk can screen them cleanly before check-in. If anything looks off, flag it at once and hold the handover until the details match the record. That includes crate condition, carrier fit, and any welfare note that affects acceptance.

We also need the usual respect-and-speed balance at the counter: acknowledge the traveler, verify the animal plan, and move on without drama. If Scout or any similar pet is on the board, keep the path quiet and avoid crowding around the crate. Thanks for staying sharp and kind with it all, and please pass along anything that needs a follow-up before the next wave starts.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
